content.text: Free Wi-Fi is everywhere now: in cafes, malls, hotels, hospitals and airports across Oman and the Gulf. It is convenient, but on an open network other people can see more of your traffic than you think. Here is what can go wrong and how to protect yourself in a few minutes.
What can go wrong on public Wi-Fi?

items: Fake hotspots: an attacker creates a network with a name like "Free Airport WiFi" or a copy of a cafe's name, and everything you send goes through their device.
Snooping: on an open network without a password, others on the same Wi-Fi can try to watch unencrypted traffic.
Fake login pages: a hotspot shows a page that looks like Google, Facebook or your bank and asks for your password.
Weak routers: old, badly set up routers can be taken over and used to redirect you to harmful sites.
1. Ask staff for the exact network name before you connect.
2. Prefer networks with a password, and never assume an open network is safe.
3. Turn on a VPN before you open any app, especially banking, email and shopping.
4. Check for the padlock and the right address in your browser before typing a password.
5. Turn on two-factor authentication for WhatsApp, email, Google and banking.
6. Turn off automatic connection to open networks and "forget" networks you no longer use.
7. Keep your phone, laptop and apps updated.
8. For banking or payments, use your mobile data if you can.

content.text: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between your device and the VPN server. Even on an open Wi-Fi network, the people around you, and even a fake hotspot, only see scrambled data instead of the sites you visit and the passwords you type. Your real IP address is hidden as well.
